candidate_sentence_map.S1: AS Tallinna Sadam Group delivered improved profitability in 2025 despite a slight decline in revenue.
candidate_sentence_map.S2: Revenue decreased by EUR 0.9 million, or 0.8%, to EUR 118.7 million, mainly because lower utilisation of the icebreaker Botnica reduced charter-fee income.
candidate_sentence_map.S3: This was partly offset by higher vessel dues, passenger fees, lease income, ferry-service revenue and cargo charges.
candidate_sentence_map.S4: Vessel dues increased 8% to EUR 34.1 million, while Botnica charter fees fell 34% to EUR 7.9 million as charter days declined by 42.
candidate_sentence_map.S5: Operating performance strengthened as expenses fell faster than revenue.
candidate_sentence_map.S6: Operating expenses decreased 10% to EUR 36.4 million, primarily because of lower maintenance and repair, lease and fuel costs, while an EUR 0.9 million insurance indemnity related to Botnica also supported results.
candidate_sentence_map.S7: Personnel expenses increased 3% to EUR 26.6 million despite the average workforce declining from 438 to 425 employees.
candidate_sentence_map.S8: Operating profit rose 12.2% to EUR 32.7 million, and the operating margin improved from 24.4% to 27.6%.
candidate_sentence_map.S9: Adjusted EBITDA increased 6.4% to EUR 56.5 million, raising the margin from 44.4% to 47.6%.
candidate_sentence_map.S10: Net profit grew 17.3% to EUR 22.5 million, while earnings per share increased from EUR 0.07 to EUR 0.09.
candidate_sentence_map.S11: Profit before income tax rose 25% to EUR 27.9 million, supported by a 30% reduction in net finance costs to EUR 4.8 million as interest rates and borrowings declined.
candidate_sentence_map.S12: The increase in net profit was moderated by higher dividend-related income tax following the abolition of Estonia’s lower tax rate for regular dividends and by the associate Green Marine reporting a loss of EUR 0.05 million, compared with a EUR 0.5 million profit in 2024.
candidate_sentence_map.S14: Cargo throughput increased 5.1% to 13.8 million tonnes, driven mainly by a 47% rise in liquid bulk and moderate growth in dry bulk, although ro-ro volumes declined 2%.
candidate_sentence_map.S15: Passenger numbers increased 1.0% to 8.3 million, with growth on the Tallinn–Helsinki route and a 25% increase in cruise passengers.
candidate_sentence_map.S16: Domestic ferry services carried 2.5 million passengers and 1.2 million vehicles, despite 0.6% fewer voyages.
candidate_sentence_map.S17: In contrast, Botnica’s utilisation rate fell to 49%, contributing to weaker revenue in the Other segment.
candidate_sentence_map.S18: The Group invested EUR 33.2 million, 14.4% less than in 2024, while operating cash flow increased to EUR 53.7 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S19: Cash and equivalents rose to EUR 32.0 million, and net debt declined 15.5% to EUR 141.7 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S20: Equity increased slightly to EUR 380.9 million, representing 61% of total assets.
candidate_sentence_map.S21: The Group paid EUR 19.2 million in dividends, or EUR 0.073 per share, and proposed the same dividend for 2025.
candidate_sentence_map.S22: Management expects moderate passenger and cargo growth in 2026 but anticipates pressure from higher input costs, financing needs and the absence of certain one-off benefits recorded in 2025.

evaluation.label: Neutral/Mixed
evaluation.justification: K1, K2, K3, K5, and K7 are PRESENT with supporting sentences identified. K4 (major strategic infrastructure investments) and K6 (adverse impact of Russia-Ukraine war) are MISSING entirely. K8 (environmental sustainability progress) is also MISSING. While HIGH importance criteria K1-K3 and K5 are covered, the missing HIGH criteria K4 and K6, plus missing MEDIUM criterion K8, result in substantial gaps that prevent a 'Generally yes' rating. The score reflects mixed coverage: key financials, passenger/cargo trends, and icebreaker performance are captured, but critical strategic, geopolitical, and sustainability context is absent.
